title: Lifeguard Application
transcript:
Speaker 0: Jane: Hello. North Bay Aquatic Center. Jane is speaking.
Speaker 1: Peter: Oh, hello. I’m calling to apply for a part time lifeguard position. Am I speaking to the right person?
Speaker 0: Jane: Yes. You are. We are currently recruiting lifeguards for two different positions. But first, I’ll have to jot down some of your personal information before we officially invite you for an interview. Is that alright?
Speaker 1: Peter: Sure. No problem.
Speaker 0: Jane: May I have your name, please?
Speaker 1: Peter: It’s Peter. Peter Smith.
Speaker 0: Jane: Okay. And what is your current address?
Speaker 1: Peter: It’s 130 South Main Street, Lake Elsinore.
Speaker 0: I’m sorry. Elsinore?
Speaker 1: Oh, it’s E L S I N 0 R E, Elsinore.
Speaker 0: Jane: Right. Got it. What is your phone number?
Speaker 1: Peter: My home phone number is 077995362. Actually, it’s easier to reach me by my cell phone number. It’s 077896245. I’m mainly out these days.
Speaker 0: Jane: Right. Can you tell me about your work experience?
Speaker 1: Peter: Well, I now work as a waiter, and that’s just a part time gig. It requires serving customers, and I also have some cleaning duties.
Speaker 0: Jane: Okay. Do you have any other part time job?
Speaker 1: Peter: No. But I’m majoring in physical education right now. I’m learning exercise physiology, sports nutrition, and individual fitness activities, and I want to become a baseball coach for a local high school.
Speaker 0: So do you have any other relevant work experience to a lifeguard position?
Speaker 1: Oh, right. I also worked part time as a rescue diver for a local beach last summer. I’m certified for open water rescue missions.
Speaker 0: Jane: Excellent. That’s exactly what we’re looking for. Jane: Before we continue, I need to know a few more things to ensure that you are qualified for maintaining water safety during work.
Speaker 1: Peter: Okay. Go ahead.
Speaker 0: Jane: As a lifeguard, you will spend most of your time monitoring the area near the water and reducing risks to everyone here. So we are looking for someone who can stay focused. Do you have difficulties concentrating or any related disorders?
Speaker 1: Peter: No. I don’t have any medical disorders relating to that sort of problem.
Speaker 0: Jane: We’re also expecting someone with good eyesight because a lifeguard must be able to recognize and respond to any struggling swimmers quickly.
Speaker 1: Peter: I have sharp vision. I mean, both eyes are twenty ten without correction.
Speaker 0: Jane: Good. Do you have relevant skills in terms of lifeguarding?
Speaker 1: Peter: I’m good at diving. You know my previous job requires training in that.
Speaker 0: Jane: We only need lifeguards with certification. I assume you already have one. Right?
Speaker 1: Peter: Yes. To get the certificate, I received training for Waterfront Lifeguarding two years ago. The training includes things like providing first aid and emergency care, but mine is about to expire in November. Oh, wait. Let me check. It’s a month earlier, in October.
Speaker 0: Jane: Okay. You’re good for now before it expires. But if you want to work here for the whole year, you’ll have to renew it.
Speaker 1: Peter: I see.
Speaker 0: Jane: What time do you prefer to work?
Speaker 1: Peter: I already work part time in a restaurant on weekdays, so I’d like to work on the weekend.
Speaker 0: Jane: We already have enough people working here on Sundays.
Speaker 1: Peter: I can work on Saturday mornings then.
Speaker 0: Jane: Right.
Speaker 1: Peter: And I can start from 06:00 in the morning. I’m a morning person.
Speaker 0: Jane: Sounds great. Where did you hear about our recruitment information from?
Speaker 1: Peter: I heard it on radio this morning while driving. I wouldn’t say I like reading newspapers.
Speaker 0: Jane: Thank you for calling. We’ll notify you about the interview details in two days.
Speaker 1: Peter: Thank you. Bye.
Speaker 0: Jane: Goodbye.
